equity_bridge.item: Interests in associates at earnings-based value (book HK$7,916m)
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim: 57.98% Grand Pharma Sphere (Sirtex/SIR-Spheres global) share of profit HK$40.5m/half; 55% Xudong Haipu HK$38.1m/half; other associates loss-making (~-HK$20m/half). Valued: GPS stake HK$2.7bn (~33x depressed share of profit, reflecting FDA HCC approval Jul-2025 and R&D-burdened earnings), Xudong Haipu HK$0.9bn (~12x share of profit), others nil. 45% of book; at book the bridge would add a further HK$1.23/share - that is the bull view of the associates, not used. No quoted fair value exists (MD&A).

equity_bridge.item: Financial assets at FVTPL + equity instruments at FVOCI
equity_bridge.note: 30 Jun 2026: FVTPL 602.5 (HK-listed equity 14.0, unlisted fund 164.1, US$48.3m convertible loan to Grand Pharma Sphere 424.4 at 7.4%) + FVOCI 178.7. Telix stake fully sold in H1 FY2026 (HK$350m at Dec-2025). Fair-value income excluded from EBITDA.
30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, up from HK$224.7m at Dec-2025 after the common-control acquisition of Yuanda Jiufu/Baoding Jiahe (RMB316m) and NCI buy-in; treated as deferred consideration/debt-like.
~10x annualised NCI profit share (H1 FY2026 HK$7.1m); NCI book HK$99.9m.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_3yr_cagr (FY2022-FY2025, HK$14,140m -> HK$17,017m); 5-yr equity 8.6% includes the FY2020-21 Telix/RDC re-rating years
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (6.4% 3yr / 8.6% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS CAGR (-15.5% / -7.4%) and owner-FCF CAGR (-45% / -36%). EPS fell because FY2024 carried a HK$676m Telix fair-value gain and FY2025 a HK$189m loss plus VBP-driven margin compression (EBITDA margin 27% FY2023 -> 19% FY2025); FCF fell on the FY2025 HK$796m intangible purchase and a receivables build (+HK$981m FY2025, +HK$665m H1 FY2026). Revenue grew; per-share earnings and cash did not.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF (OCF - PPE - intangibles): SBC zero, interest income not stripped (net debt). Owner FCF HK$m: FY2020 1,197; FY2021 1,469; FY2022 785; FY2023 1,937; FY2024 1,301; FY2025 127. FY2022-25 average ~1,040 (8.9% of revenue) is the better anchor than FY2025.

scenario_narratives.base: The VBP shock to the legacy cardio-emergency and ENT books is largely absorbed as management claims, but not reversed: the sales-force reset holds H1 FY2026 cost savings while revenue grows mid-single digits in FY2026 and ~7% for three years as YiGanTai (FDA HCC approval Jul-2025) scales from the new Chengdu plant, biotech amino acids keep growing, and innovative/barrier products climb past 50% of revenue. EBITDA margin recovers from 18.7% to 21.5%, not to FY2023's 27%, because further VBP rounds keep eating the generic tail and in-licensed launches carry heavy promotion. Licensing spend recurs at ~2.5% of revenue and receivables keep absorbing a quarter of incremental revenue. The associates are worth materially less than their HK$7.9bn book on what they earn today.
scenario_narratives.bull: The radiopharma thesis lands: TLX591-CDx is approved in China in 2026, ITM-11 and TLX250-CDx follow, GPN01530 progresses under FDA Fast Track, and YiGanTai keeps its ~15x-in-four-years trajectory. Innovative products pass 65% of revenue, VBP becomes a rounding error, growth runs at double digits through FY2030 and EBITDA margin returns to 25% as distribution spend scales. Receivables normalise. The bull value still carries the associates at 45% of book; marking Sirtex/GPS at book would add ~HK$1.2/share on top.
scenario_narratives.bear: VBP keeps widening (the 12th round's ~RMB60bn across 65 categories reaches more of the respiratory/emergency portfolio), the ENT/cardio-emergency declines of H1 FY2026 prove structural rather than a sales-strategy blip, and the radiopharma pipeline slips into 2028+ with TheraSphere competing hard on Y-90. Revenue grows 2-3%, EBITDA margin slides to 17%, receivables stretch further (35% capture) as hospital payment cycles lengthen, and licensing spend stays high to refill the pipeline. Leverage (gearing ~29% of equity) is serviceable but dividends (HK$0.9bn paid FY2025, HK$0.6bn in H1 FY2026) run ahead of owner FCF.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the consolidated pharma operating business on owner FCF (no SBC exists to expense), and value the equity-accounted Sirtex/Grand Pharma Sphere and Xudong Haipu stakes separately on what they earn, not at book. Reported EPS is noise from the Telix mark-to-market (now fully exited); the question is whether VBP-adjusted operating margins and receivables stabilise. The market at the time of valuation is pricing roughly the bear-to-base path.
key_risks_to_valuation: Associate value (HK$3.6bn in the bridge, ~HK$1.03/share) is a judgment with no quoted price; at book it would be HK$2.26/share, at zero it would remove HK$1.03/share.

Receivables: +HK$1.65bn in 18 months against ~HK$0.6bn of revenue growth. If this is channel stuffing or collection weakness rather than mix, the WC capture is too mild and owner FCF stays near FY2025's HK$127m.
Licensing/M&A spend: modelled at ~2.5% of revenue; FY2024 also spent HK$1.18bn on subsidiary acquisitions and FY2025 HK$0.32bn, which the model does not charge as recurring.
Further VBP rounds hitting the respiratory/emergency franchise.
RMB/HKD translation: ~84% of cash and nearly all operations are RMB; the group does not hedge.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4.53-8.97
data_sources.financials: 0512.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, HKD millions); FY2025 Annual Report consolidated statements (income statement p.~88, cash flow p.91, share award scheme p.71); H1 FY2026 Interim Report (balance sheet pp.66-68, cash flow p.70, notes 11-12, MD&A significant investments p.51)

inputs.sbc_source: Zero, genuinely: FY2025 AR p.71 - no share option scheme adopted, no options outstanding; the 2021 Share Award Scheme trust holds 47,761,500 treasury shares bought for HK$268.5m but 'the Group did not grant any awards'. SBC-zero market; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z (HKEX regular close, Friday; Yahoo chart API)
inputs.share_count_basis: Issued 3,549.57m (share capital HK$35,496k at HK$0.01) less 47.76m treasury shares held by the share-award trust = 3,501.8m. Diluted EPS equals basic (H1 FY2026 interim note 8); no options or convertibles outstanding. Held flat: no SBC, no buybacks since FY2023, no equity raises.
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD reporting currency, economically RMB flows (HKD pegged to USD; ~84% of cash RMB). Risk-free 3.6% (10y HKGB/UST proxy); ERP 7.5% (mature-market 5% plus ~2.5pp China country premium, since the operations, customers and regulator are all Mainland); beta 1.0 -> cost of equity ~11.1%. Bank debt ~HK$5.0bn at 2.2-4.98% (FY2025 AR), ~3.0% after tax, ~23% of capital at market -> WACC ~9.2%, rounded to 9.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: VBP and pipeline risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not via a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities HK$53.7m (current 11.7 + non-current 42.0, 30 Jun 2026) included in net debt; lease principal (HK$21.7m FY2025) NOT deducted from flows. Immaterial either way (<0.3% of EV).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI is ~0.7% of profit (H1 FY2026 HK$7.1m of HK$1,068.6m). Charged once, in the equity bridge at ~10x NCI profit share (HK$140m vs book HK$99.9m).
inputs.net_debt_build: 30 Jun 2026: bank and other borrowings 1,666.2 current + 3,331.1 non-current = 4,997.4; lease liabilities 53.7; total debt 5,051.1. Cash 623.1 + pledged deposits 43.6 = 666.7. Net debt 4,384.4.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF component route with the non-US adaptations (HKD WACC, one lease treatment, NCI once, associates/investments in the bridge with their income excluded from the flows, SBC-zero). Grand Pharma is a consolidated operating pharma group (branded/generic pharma, biotech amino acids, nuclear medicine, cardiovascular devices) - not a bank/REIT/holdco - so owner FCF is the right stream. Its large equity-accounted associates (58% of Grand Pharma Sphere/Sirtex, 55% of Xudong Haipu; HK$7.9bn book) are valued separately in the bridge; 'share of results of associates' and FVTPL changes (Telix, now fully sold) are excluded from EBITDA, matching the bridge. FCF BASE: reported FCF FY2025 = OCF 1,649.5 - PPE 726.2 - intangibles 796.0 = 127.4 (the HK$796m intangible purchase is in-licensing/product rights; the build charges licensing as a recurring ~2.5% of revenue inside capex rather than as a one-off). Interest income (HK$7.4m) not stripped: the company is net debt, not net cash. Interest paid sits in financing, so OCF is pre-interest and consistent with discounting at WACC and deducting net debt once. TIMING: FY0 is FY2025 but net debt is the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet; H1 FY2026 FCF (-HK$89.5m, seasonally weak H1 as in FY2024/25) has already passed through that balance sheet while year 1 of the projection is full FY2026 - a mild overstatement of ~half a year's H1 flow (small, < HK$0.03/share). No buybacks since FY2023 (HK$81m); flat share count needs no funding because there is no SBC.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +5%: H1 FY2026 +3.2% on restated base (+4.6% vs originally-reported H1 FY2025), nuclear medicine +55%, biotech +34%, ENT -25% and cardio-emergency -12% on the sales-force reset; RMB translation tailwind in H2. FY2027-29 7% as innovative/barrier products (~50% of revenue) outgrow the VBP-exposed legacy book, decelerating to 3.5% by FY2035.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 operating EBITDA ~HK$2,351m (18.7%) after VBP price cuts and HK$3.8bn distribution spend; H1 FY2026 ~23% after a HK$337m distribution-cost cut, but H2 is seasonally weaker (H2 FY2025 ~14%). FY2026 19.5%, recovering to 21.5% by FY2030 on mix - still well below FY2023's 27% because VBP keeps recurring.
base.capex_rationale: PPE ~4% (Chengdu radiopharma plant completed Jun-2025; FY2023-25 4.6-5.9%) plus ~2.5% of revenue for recurring in-licensing/product-rights purchases (FY2022 HK$431m, FY2025 HK$796m; the in-licensing model is the growth engine, so it is a recurring cost, not a one-off).
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer/distributor to Chinese hospitals: receivables + inventory - payables ~22% of revenue and stretching (receivables +HK$1.2bn FY2025, +HK$665m H1 FY2026). Growth consumes ~25% of incremental revenue.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 21% of operating EBIT FY2024 (480/2,285), ~20% FY2025 (354/1,769); PRC high-tech 15% subsidiaries blended with 25% statutory.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: a single regulator (NHSA via VBP) sets prices on much of the legacy book, two segments declined double digits in H1 FY2026, and FY2025 owner FCF was only HK$127m with receivables still building. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (China RDC approvals, YiGanTai scale-up, VBP fading, receivables normalising). Base held at 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
